• Gita attends in April.
• Jaya attends before Kiran.
• Exactly 6 interview slots fall between the interviews of Riya and Esha.

Statements: Only a few files are cheques. All cheques are loans. No loans is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are not cheques.
II. No cheques is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are cheques. Some cheques are loans. All loans are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All files are bonds.
II. No cheques is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some files are cheques. All cheques are loans. No loans is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are loans.
II. Some cheques are bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No files is a cheques. Some cheques are loans. All loans are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All files are bonds.
II. Some bonds are cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

Conclusions: I. U ≥ Q   II. V > Q.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
credit secure savings = re lu ka
credit digital access = ze re pa
secure digital rural = lu pa su
savings access rural = su ze ka
credit secure rural = re su lu
What is the code for “credit”?
questions.explanation: Answer: re. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: credit = re, secure = lu, savings = ka, digital = pa, access = ze, rural = su.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 29 km west, turns right and walks 36 km, then turns right and walks 14 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 39. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 15 km along the initial direction and 36 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(15² + 36²) = 39 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 38 km north, turns left and walks 36 km, then turns left and walks 23 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 75 km south, turns left and walks 105 km, then turns left and walks 19 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: A is the mother of C. F is the daughter of C. B is the father of C. How is F related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. B is a parent of C, and F is C’s daughter. Hence F is B’s grandchild.

questions.stem: D is the brother of H. H is the mother of B. E is the father of D and H. How is D related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. D is the brother of B’s mother H. Therefore D is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: C is the only daughter of E. E is the father of C. A is the son of C. B is the sister of E. How is E related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. E is the father of C, and C is A’s mother. Thus E is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 58 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 46. New front rank = 10+3 = 13. Back rank = 58 − 13 + 1 = 46.

questions.stem: In a queue of 36 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 23. New front rank = 10+4 = 14. Back rank = 36 − 14 + 1 = 23.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2100 each. One earns 25% profit and the other incurs 20% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 4305. Recover each cost separately: 2100×100/125 + 2100×100/80. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 42 and 63 hours. An outlet empties it in 105 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.16. Net rate = 1/42 + 1/63 − 1/105 = 19/630 tank/hour. Required time = 33.16 hours.

questions.stem: A boat covers 130 km in still water in 10 hours. If the stream flows at 4 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 5 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. Still-water speed = 13 km/h. Upstream speed = 13 − 4. Distance = speed × 5.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 7:4. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 8 months. A receives ₹235200 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 324800. Profit ratio is 84:32. Each ratio unit = ₹2800. Total = 116 × 2800.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹19000 earns ₹2850 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 20947.5. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 5%. Compound amount = 19000 × (1 + 5/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 180 litres of pure milk. 36 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 115.2. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 180 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 13 people is 58 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 72. New total minus old total = (13+1)×(58+1) − 13×58 = 72.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 9 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 27. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+9)/(x+9) = 3/2 gives x = 9. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 190 m train moving at 72 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 7.2 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 10.56. Relative speed = (72 − 7.2) ×5/18 = 18 m/s. Time = 190/18.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 20%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹1600. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 16.67. New quantity / old quantity = 100/120. Reduction percentage = 20/120 ×100.
